The other Glottolog refs attached to the target record (Hebei fangyan zhi 2005; Wen Yu 1941 on Qiang; Jinping Han-Dong-Miao fangyan zhi 2008; Wenshan minzu zhi 2005) are gazetteer/unrelated items, not Muji descriptions.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 3.3 'Southern Muji phonology in brief' (pp. 8-9): {(C)(V)VT} template, segment inventory, 'five pitch contrasts: high-level /55/, mid-level /33/, low-rising /13/, low-falling /21/ and, high-falling /52/', sandhi [22-21]/[22-21-21], tense voice as co-articulation of /21/ and /13/, non-contrastive nasalization. The words stress/accent occur nowhere in the book; refers to Pelkey (2011, De Gruyter) for the full sketch.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-120: split [ymj] Muji Yi into [ymc] Southern Muji, [ymx] Northern Muji, [ymq] Qila Muji, [ymi] Moji, [ymz] Muzi (submitted by J. R. Pelkey; adopted 2008-01-14).
sources.note: Nothing; identity/intelligibility rationale only; sole source cited is Pelkey 2008 PhD.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Muji's mirrored merger: correlative redistribution of checked tone classes in a newly defined Burmic cluster. Mon-Khmer Studies 37: 179-195.
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 2 'Sample phonology sketch' (pp. 181-183) describes Muji-PJZ (= Southern Muji, Pujiazhai): syllable C(V)VT, 34 initials, 9 monophthongs + 9 diphthongs, five contrastive tones 55/33/13/21/52 with pitch plots, sandhi rules (/21/>[22] before 21, /21/>[52] etc.), phonation non-contrastive but co-occurring with tones 21 and 13. No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the article (scanned grep + pages read).

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. Dialectology as Dialectic: Interpreting Phula Variation. TiLSM 229. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
